build: Software Projects disk, alternate D64 with LA–LJ files

exclude: Disk staging for bytes copied to $1E00 and graphics decoded to $4000; disk tail remains in the queue.
extra: Scene bytes copied by the runtime loader
Tail of the file loaded at $8010, role unresolved

comments.text: The first copied byte in the scene record is $01. The caller starts executing one byte later.

Save and reload the caller stack pointer, install the shared raster handler and configure the hallway colours. Convert screen cells at $4000 through the colour table at $7700, copy the digit glyphs, select character mode pointers and initialize sprites.
Copy the 90-byte table at $3200 to $44–$9D with X counting down from $59.
Wait for two CIA2 timer periods, then update the hallway. If $2D23 is set, enable all eight sprites. Dispatch the $2D25 path or poll the action routines beginning at $274A.
Start a 25-pass transition countdown. At count $11 call $2ABA with A=5, and call $28B8 on each pass.
Select pose 5, wait ten periods and reset the sprite positions. Subtract $14 from five sprite Y coordinates and let the next approach advance while checking input and its timing flags.
Install $2CA3 as raster target, configure the upper four sprites and time a 25-pass animation. Switch the table selector when the counter reaches $11.
Clear sprite high X, set colours for sprites 1–3 and select their graphics and initial positions. The next input window starts after the delay at $2291.
Poll for changed joystick input on each of six timer periods. An exact fire mask takes the animation at $2308. Timeout changes the sprite set and jumps to the failure delay at $2713.
Set the mirror flag and load pointers $63 and $5E through the sprite transformation routine. Place the sprites from the table at $2E41.
Check six timer periods for the same fire mask as the first jump window. Valid input branches to $245B. Otherwise install the missed-jump position and pose before the failure delay.
Update the moving sprites each period and accept a new exact joystick mask $02 within the seven-period window. The timeout path uses the coordinate table at $3197.
Update the moving sprites and look for a change to the exact right mask $08 within ten timer periods. If the counter expires use the coordinate table at $319F and go to $2713.
Write $FF to CIA1 port A, invert the joystick sample and compare it with the previous active-high sample. Retain the new sample at $28.
Wait A times using the resident two-period timer routine. Read the joystick between waits.
For A iterations wait, sample the joystick and step the four moving sprites through $276F.
Wait and sample the joystick A times, calling the periodic encounter update at $28B8.
Wait and read the joystick A times. Call $29AE between waits to advance the pair of animated sprites.
Initialize five coordinate pairs from $2CFB, copy initial motion flags and frame pointers, set the sprite colours and clear the encounter flags before setting high X for sprites 0 and 1.
Compute 90 times A, add $3200 and copy that pose record to $44–$9D after synchronizing to the lower half of the raster.
Use A to index an 18-byte record at $305B. Copy positions for sprites 4–7, four colors and four pointers, then combine the high nibble expansion masks with the existing low nibbles.
Select the next raster target at $2B70 and its line from $99. Apply the first band position, pointer, colour and expansion values to sprites 5–7.
Select the third raster update and line from $9A. Load the second band sprite positions from $50–$55, colours and pointers before restoring the expansion set.
Apply the third band sprite record and select the next handler at $2BEA on the line in $9B.
Select the fifth raster band using line $9C, then apply sprite coordinates from $68–$6D and pointer values from $71–$73.

Read active-high joystick masks and return the sample on an exact match to A. No movement and samples suppressed during cooldown return $FF. An incorrect nonzero mask also queues sound $89 and starts the 20-call cooldown.
This scene record ends with the eleven byte marker copied by the unpacker at $0DDE.
The first page of the screen matrix for the background in VIC bank $4000. Its character codes index the scene colour lookup when the display is initialized.
Screen matrix offsets $100–$1FF. The VIC reads these as character codes and the palette routine processes a page at a time.
Screen matrix offsets $200–$2FF. The screen maps into the glyph data at $7800.
The last page of the screen matrix, including the hardware sprite pointers at $43F8–$43FF.
The first two rendered hallway sprite fragments immediately before the pair loaded into sprites 5 and 6.
Two consecutive 64-byte sprite records selected by hardware sprites 5 and 6 in the Skull Hallway play capture, using VIC pointers $12 and $13.
Sixteen adjacent sprite frames. Rendering the uncompressed records shows torso, head and leg fragments in different poses for the hallway animation.
The next sixteen sprite pieces, including extended arms and rounded head fragments.
A run of 16 sprite pieces with bent or straight legs and the companion upper-body pieces.
Sprite pieces include extended steps in the early records and small torso and head fragments in the later records.
Mid-range hallway animation shapes. The code selects pointer $63 for sprite 1 at $225E.
Adjacent body and face sprite pieces. The animation sets pointer $6F at $2296 and $68 at $229E.
Sixteen 64-byte sprite slots including the fragment selected by the immediate pointer $74 at $22DD.
Sprite slots including the mask pointed to by sprite 1 when $22D7 writes $85. Several consecutive images show falling body poses.
Rendered shapes include angled legs and drifting silhouettes in 64-byte steps.
A run of limb silhouettes, including the $A9 sprite selected by the routine at $20CF.
The sixteen shapes around pointer $C0, which is selected for sprite 3 at $22E7.
The final compact bank of individual sprite pieces begins at pointer $C4 and includes legs, a torso and a moving overhead figure.
The unpacked picture stream initializes $73FF–$7611 to zero. These bytes are still zero in the play capture.
Table indexed by the screen cell at $4000–$43FF during initialization. Each entry supplies the colour RAM nibble for that cell.
The scene character glyph store for VIC bank $4000 and character-base bits 3–1 of $D018 set to 7. A character occupies eight consecutive bytes.
The top half of this scene set, from character code $80. The eight-byte glyph slots are used for the scene-specific objects and screen details.
Repeated $02 bytes at $BD22–$BF0F, after the input consumed by the scene picture decode.
